messages:
emma: quick question — running into flaky behavior when streaming from the RN app. We start a streaming generation via the hosted API, then the app refreshes the auth token (short-lived jwt) and the stream immediately aborts. Is that expected? anyone seen best practice?

sam-mobile: yep seen this. RN networking libs (fetch/XHR) will fail if you mutate auth mid-request. streaming is tied to the original request headers.

jun: correct. once the HTTP connection is open, changing the token client-side doesn't change the server's auth context. if you rotate mid-stream you'll need to reopen the stream. for long-running streams use a session-level auth (cookie or long-lived ephemeral token) or websocket/SSE authenticated at connect time.

nate: fwiw the runtime will reject requests with expired tokens. we don't currently support transparent mid-stream token refresh — this is tracked in issue #3241 (auto-refresh-token for streams). short-term patterns:
- avoid rotating tokens while a stream is active
- open streams with a token that will remain valid for the expected duration (e.g., 60s)
- use a refresh handshake before streaming starts

olivia: practical RN tips: if you're using react-native-webview to proxy a native stream into the app, ensure the webview has the same cookie store or pass a signed ephemeral token into the webview URL param (but be careful with URL leak).

emma: thanks. any examples for doing the handshake or fallback approach?

sam-mobile: example pattern — request a short-lived stream token from backend (server-side exchanges refresh token), then start the stream with that token. if the user needs > token lifetime, reopen the stream with a new token and append to UI.

sam-mobile: JS fetch streaming example:

```js
const res = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${streamToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  // keepalive helps for background, but doesn't change header semantics
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // append chunk to UI
}
```

sam-mobile: note: if your RN app uses the fetch polyfill that routes to native networking, you might lose streaming (no ReadableStream). In that case use websocket or a native module wrapper.

jun: iOS native note: URLSession dataTask will use the header values at time of connect. don't mutate headers across the same task. Swift example to set auth at connect time:

```swift
var req = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream")!)
req.setValue("Bearer \(token)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Authorization")
let task = URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: req) { data, resp, err in
  // stream come in chunks via delegate if using dataTask with delegate
}
task.resume()
```

nate: Kotlin/OkHttp tip: attach an Interceptor that refreshes tokens only for idempotent/non-streaming requests. For streaming endpoints, the interceptor should not try to silently refresh mid-call — instead fail and let the client reopen.

olivia: small CORS gotcha we've hit in webview-in-web scenarios: if you authenticate with cookies, the host must set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and the fetch must use credentials: 'include'. Also ensure Access-Control-Expose-Headers includes any custom headers you need.

emma: thanks — what about SSE vs chunked fetch vs websocket? pros/cons for RN + Swift/Kotlin wrappers?

sam-mobile: websocket = most robust for RN native wrappers (binary friendly, reconnect strategies). SSE (EventSource) works well on web but RN has spotty EventSource support. chunked fetch (Readablestream) is simplest on browsers but tricky in RN because polyfills often drop streaming.

jun: summary:
- Browser: chunked fetch or SSE fine if CORS/credentials are correct.
- RN JS layer: prefer websocket or a native streaming module.
- Native iOS/Android: URLSession/OkHttp streaming works, but authenticate at connect time and reopen on token rotation.

ci-bot: deploy note — we've added a flag to the dev cluster to extend stream-token TTL to 90s for integration tests this week. See CI run: https://ci.internal/runs/1122

nate: FYI we're going to add an explicit error code for "token_expired_during_stream" in the next runtime release so clients can auto-detect and reopen cleanly. RFC in PR #4532 coming soon.

emma: perfect — I'll implement the handshake flow on mobile and wire up reconnection to UI. will ping when I have a draft PR. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
